name: Unilateral CVA (no wrong-way risk, netting or collateral)
prompt: How is unilateral CVA computed from the counterparty's loss severity, the discounted exposure profile and the default probabilities over each future interval?

variables.meaning: unilateral credit value adjustment; a negative number (a reduction in portfolio value)
loss given default of the counterparty (decimal)
number of future time intervals
discounted expected positive exposure at future date t_i
marginal default probability of the counterparty over the interval from t_{i-1} to t_i (decimal)

corruptions.why: The leading minus sign is dropped; in the notes CVA is a negative number, a reduction in the value of the portfolio.
Loss severity is LGD = 1 - RR, not the recovery rate; a higher recovery must reduce CVA.
Each interval must use the marginal default probability over that interval, not the cumulative probability from today.

sensitivities.why: A larger loss severity makes CVA more negative, i.e. a bigger charge.
More exposure at risk at each date makes CVA more negative.
A higher chance of default in any interval makes CVA more negative.

intuition: Loss severity times, date by date, what they would owe you times the chance they default right then, booked as a cost.

name: Unilateral CVA as a running spread (constant EPE)
prompt: Under a constant-EPE assumption, how is CVA expressed as a per annum running spread using only the counterparty's credit spread and the exposure?

variables.meaning: CVA of the position over t to T; dividing by the CDS premium term turns it into a running (per annum) spread
CDS premium term over t to T; dividing CVA(t,T) by it expresses CVA as a per annum running spread
the counterparty's CDS spread
average expected positive exposure, assumed constant over time

corruptions.why: CVA is a negative number (a charge), so the running spread carries a minus sign.
The LGD-and-default-probability apparatus already collapses into the credit spread; multiplying by LGD again double counts.
CVA is driven by positive exposure (what the counterparty owes you); ENE belongs to DVA.

sensitivities.why: A wider counterparty spread makes the running CVA charge more negative.
More average exposure makes the running CVA charge more negative.

intuition: Per year, CVA is just the counterparty's credit spread charged on the average amount they owe you.

name: Implied hazard rate from the credit spread and recovery rate
prompt: What default intensity is implied by a counterparty's credit spread once you allow for its recovery rate?

variables.meaning: implied hazard rate (default intensity) of the counterparty
credit spread of the counterparty
recovery rate (decimal); 1 - RR is the LGD

corruptions.why: The spread compensates for the loss given default, 1 - RR, not for the recovery.
The spread is divided by LGD, not multiplied: s = lambda x LGD, so lambda = s / LGD.

sensitivities.why: A wider spread implies a higher default intensity.
A higher recovery shrinks the denominator 1 - RR and raises the implied PD (even though CVA itself falls, because LGD falls faster).

intuition: Spread pays for expected loss, so strip out the loss severity to get the default rate: more recovery means more defaults are needed to justify the same spread.

name: Bilateral CVA (BCVA) as CVA plus DVA
prompt: How is bilateral CVA assembled from its two components?

variables.meaning: bilateral CVA, admitting both parties' defaults
counterparty-default component (negative: a cost)
debt value adjustment, own-default component (positive: a benefit)

corruptions.why: In this reading's convention CVA is already negative and DVA already positive, so the two are simply added.
Dropping DVA gives unilateral CVA; BCVA is UCVA plus the DVA term.

sensitivities.why: BCVA moves one-for-one with the CVA term.
A larger DVA benefit makes BCVA less negative.

intuition: Your cost from their default plus your benefit from your own default.

name: BCVA component: CVA (counterparty-default term)

number of future time intervals
discounted expected positive exposure at date t_i

corruptions.why: The CVA term uses the counterparty's default probability; the institution's own PD belongs in DVA.

sensitivities.why: Higher counterparty loss severity makes CVA more negative.
More positive exposure makes CVA more negative.
A riskier counterparty makes CVA more negative.

intuition: Subscript C everywhere: their severity, their default probability, on what they owe you.

name: BCVA component: DVA (own-default term)

ENE rising toward zero (owing the counterparty less) shrinks the DVA benefit.

intuition: Mirror image of CVA with subscript I: your severity and your default probability on what you owe them; minus times negative ENE makes it a gain.

name: Converting standalone CVA into a running spread on a swap
prompt: To build CVA into a swap's pricing as a per annum spread, what do you divide the standalone CVA by?
